questions.stem: The state of a substance depends on the balance between:

options.text: The number of atoms and molecules
The kinetic energy of particles and the forces of attraction between them

questions.explanation: The state depends on the balance between particle kinetic energy (which tends to separate particles) and the attractive forces between them (which tend to hold them together).

questions.stem: Which property is true of liquids but NOT solids?

options.text: They can flow and take the shape of their container

questions.explanation: Liquids can flow and take the shape of their container because particles can move past each other. Solids have a fixed shape.

questions.stem: Gases can be easily compressed because:

options.text: Gas particles have strong forces between them
There are large spaces between gas particles

questions.explanation: Gases can be compressed easily because there are large spaces between the particles, allowing them to be pushed closer together.

questions.stem: Why do solids generally have a higher density than gases?

options.text: Solid particles are closely packed together, so more mass is in the same volume

questions.explanation: In solids, particles are closely packed in a regular arrangement, resulting in many more particles (and therefore more mass) per unit volume than in gases.

questions.stem: Which state of matter has no fixed shape and no fixed volume?
questions.explanation: Gases have no fixed shape and no fixed volume. They expand to fill any container because their particles move freely and are far apart.

questions.stem: In which state do particles have the strongest forces of attraction between them?

options.text: Forces are equal in all states

questions.explanation: Solids have the strongest forces of attraction between particles, which is why they hold their shape and cannot flow.

questions.stem: Why are liquids and solids both described as incompressible?

options.text: Because their particles do not move
Because their particles are already close together with little space between them
Because they have the same density

questions.explanation: In both solids and liquids, particles are already close together with very little space between them, so they cannot be pushed significantly closer.
